uncited: Visibility Culling is a family of acceleration techniques in volume rendering that reduces computational load by identifying and bypassing data or primitives that do not contribute to the final image.

It sets itself apart from its siblings by encompassing a broad range of strategies—from geometric frustum tests to optical termination and screen-space feedback—unlike [Bounding Volume Empty-Space Culling](17140-bounding-volume-empty-space-culling.md) which focuses strictly on geometric emptiness, or [Parallel Ray Casting with Segment Lists](2565-parallel-ray-casting-with-segment-lists.md) which focuses on parallelization efficiency.
**Culling/Skipping:** Identifying regions of the volume or ray path that do not contribute to the final image (e.g., empty space, occluded voxels) and bypassing their evaluation.
